short: Rwanda has no AI law. It has a non-binding National AI Policy from the ICT ministry and a binding personal data protection law, Law No. 058/2021, whose Article 21 restricts decisions based solely on automated processing.
title: Rwanda AI Laws
subtitle: No AI law: a national AI policy and the personal data protection law
body_html:
Status at a glance

No AI law. Rwanda has a National AI Policy from the Ministry of ICT and Innovation (MINICT), which is not binding, and a binding personal data protection law, Law No. 058/2021 of 13 October 2021, whose Article 21 gives a right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing. Verified on 25 October 2026 against MINICT, the Ministry of Justice's Official Gazette and the Data Protection and Privacy Office.

Key instruments

InstrumentNumberDateLegal force
The National AI PolicyMINICTNo date is printed in the documentPolicy
Law relating to the protection of personal data and privacyLaw No. 058/2021 of 13/10/2021Official Gazette No. Special of 15/10/2021Binding; two years' transition for existing operators (Art. 67)

Who regulates and enforces

  • National Cyber Security Authority, through its Data Protection and Privacy Office: the supervisory authority under Law No. 058/2021.
  • MINICT and the Rwanda Utilities Regulatory Authority (RURA): authors of the AI policy; RURA leads its practical ethical guidelines.

Scope and reach

Law No. 058/2021 applies to controllers, processors and third parties established or resident in Rwanda, and to those not established there that process the personal data of data subjects located in Rwanda (Art. 2).

Core obligations

  • A right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that has legal or similarly significant effects, except with consent, under a contract, or where a law provides safeguards (Art. 21).
  • The AI policy's six priority areas, including practical AI ethical guidelines, are not binding.

Penalties

BreachMaximumProvisionEnforcer
Administrative misconduct under the data protection lawNot less than RWF 2,000,000 and not more than RWF 5,000,000, or 1% of the global turnover of the preceding financial year; the text does not say which applies whenLaw No. 058/2021, Art. 53Supervisory authority

What is coming next

No AI bill has been announced. Cabinet decisions and the Official Gazette are watched weekly.

How the policy is meant to work

Cabinet approved the National AI Policy on 20 April 2023, as Access Partnership, the OECD.AI policy navigator and Digital Policy Alert all record; the Cabinet communiqué itself was not found. MINICT wrote it with the Rwanda Utilities Regulatory Authority (RURA), GIZ FAIR Forward, the Centre for the Fourth Industrial Revolution Rwanda (C4IR, the first African node of the World Economic Forum network, agreed at Davos in 2020) and The Future Society. It is organised around six priority areas and seven ethical principles, requires every AI system to comply with Law No. 058/2021, and gives RURA the role of technical regulator with power to act against a system that breaches the ethical AI guidelines, which RURA is to develop. The National Cyber Security Authority, which houses the Data Protection and Privacy Office, enforces the data side. The policy proposed a Responsible AI Office inside MINICT and costed implementation at about USD 76.5 million over five years; the University of Melbourne's Pursuit reported in 2026 that only USD 1.2 million had been mobilised as of 2023 and that the office had not opened.

On 8 June 2026 Cabinet, meeting under President Kagame, approved the creation of a National Artificial Intelligence Agency, Rwanda's first institution dedicated to AI, which takes over the responsibilities of the AI Office within MINICT and is to work from the national data centre with a governed data sandbox giving researchers and firms access to local datasets. The New Times and KT Press reported it on the day; the government said the agency builds on C4IR rather than replacing it. The founding law or decree that would give the agency legal personality had not been gazetted when this page was checked, so its powers are not yet known.

For a deployer the practical position is unchanged: no AI-specific duties bind, Law No. 058/2021 does, and a company registering with the Data Protection and Privacy Office should expect RURA's ethical AI guidelines, when published, to be the reference the new agency uses.

4 November 2026, against the sources above. The Cabinet approval dates of 20 April 2023 and 8 June 2026 are as the OECD navigator, Access Partnership and the Rwandan press report them; neither appears in a communiqué this site could read, so both are reported rather than verified.
